tools.description:

    Use this first to resolve city names, postal codes or coordinates into
    place_id values for the other weather tools. Provide either `query`

tools.name: get_forecast
tools.description:
Weather forecast for up to 20 locations in one call.

    Sections (comma-separated): 'current' (now), 'hourly' (up to 168 h ahead,
    trimmed to `hours`), 'daily' (up to 30 days ahead, trimmed to `days`),
    'minutely' (precipitation minute-by-minute, higher tiers), 'alerts'

tools.name: get_alerts
tools.description:
Official weather warnings (severe weather alerts) for up to 20 locations.

    Returns only locations that currently have an active alert, with event
    type, severity, validity window and headline — an empty list means all
    clear. Cheap to call frequently; designed for monitoring/polling.
    C

tools.name: get_weather_history
tools.description:
Historical weather (archive) with server-side aggregation.

    The archive holds 20 years, but how much of it a key may read depends on
    its plan: startup includes the last 7 days, standard the last year,
    premium and flexi all 20 years; byvalue reaches 366 days back and no
    further. Older

tools.name: get_air_quality
tools.description:
Hourly air-quality (smog) forecast for up to 20 locations, about 4 days ahead.

    Columns: `air_quality` (index, 1 = good, higher = worse) and pollutant
    surface concentrations — default pm10, pm25, no2_surface, so2_surface,
    ozone_surface; also available via `variables`: co_surface, no_surf

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_weather_history" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.
